sentences.en: Good morning. How are you? (Audience) Good.
sentences.zh: 早上好。你好吗？ （观众）好。

sentences.en: It's been great, hasn't it? I've been blown away by the whole thing.
sentences.zh: 太棒了，不是吗？我对整件事感到震惊。

sentences.en: In fact, I'm leaving. (Laughter) There have been three themes running through the conference, which are relevant to what I want to talk about.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我要走了。 （笑声）整个会议贯穿了三个主题，这三个主题与我想讲的内容相关。

sentences.en: One is the extraordinary evidence of human creativity in all of the presentations that we've had and in all of the people here; just the variety of it and the range of it.
sentences.zh: 一是我们所做的所有演讲以及在座的所有人都证明了人类创造力的非凡证据；只是它的种类和范围。

sentences.en: The second is that it's put us in a place where we have no idea what's going to happen in terms of the future.
sentences.zh: 第二，它让我们处于一个不知道未来会发生什么的境地。

sentences.en: No idea how this may play out. I have an interest in education.
sentences.zh: 不知道这会如何发展。我对教育感兴趣。

sentences.en: Actually, what I find is, everybody has an interest in education.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我发现每个人都对教育感兴趣。

sentences.en: Don't you? I find this very interesting.
sentences.zh: 不是吗？我觉得这很有趣。

sentences.en: If you're at a dinner party, and you say you work in education -- actually, you're not often at dinner parties, frankly.
sentences.zh: 如果你在一个晚宴上，你说你从事教育工作——坦率地说，实际上，你并不经常参加晚宴。

sentences.en: (Laughter) If you work in education, you're not asked.
sentences.zh: （笑声）如果你从事教育工作，就不会被问到。

sentences.en: (Laughter) And you're never asked back, curiously. That's strange to me.
sentences.zh: （笑声） 奇怪的是，你从来没有被问过。这对我来说很奇怪。

sentences.en: But if you are, and you say to somebody, you know, they say, "What do you do?"
sentences.zh: 但如果你是，你对某人说，你知道，他们会说，“你是做什么的？”

sentences.en: and you say you work in education, you can see the blood run from their face.
sentences.zh: 你说你从事教育工作，你可以看到他们脸上流着血。

sentences.en: They're like, "Oh my God. Why me?" (Laughter) "My one night out all week."
sentences.zh: 他们就像，“天哪。为什么是我？” （笑声） “我这一周都出去玩了一晚。”

sentences.en: (Laughter) But if you ask about their education, they pin you to the wall, because it's one of those things that goes deep with people, am I right?
sentences.zh: （笑声）但是如果你问起他们的教育，他们会把你钉在墙上，因为这是人们深入人心的事情之一，我说得对吗？

sentences.en: Like religion and money and other things.
sentences.zh: 比如宗教、金钱和其他东西。

sentences.en: So I have a big interest in education, and I think we all do.
sentences.zh: 所以我对教育非常感兴趣，我想我们都是如此。

sentences.en: We have a huge vested interest in it, partly because it's education that's meant to take us into this future that we can't grasp.
sentences.zh: 我们对它有着巨大的既得利益，部分原因是教育旨在带我们进入我们无法掌握的未来。

sentences.en: If you think of it, children starting school this year will be retiring in 2065.
sentences.zh: 如果你想一想，今年开始上学的孩子们将于 2065 年退休。

sentences.en: Nobody has a clue, despite all the expertise that's been on parade for the past four days, what the world will look like in five years' time.
sentences.zh: 尽管过去四天里大家都在展示各种专业知识，但没有人知道五年后的世界会是什么样子。

sentences.en: And yet, we're meant to be educating them for it.
sentences.zh: 然而，我们应该为此教育他们。

sentences.en: So the unpredictability, I think, is extraordinary.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，不可预测性是非同寻常的。

sentences.en: And the third part of this is that we've all agreed, nonetheless, on the really extraordinary capacities that children have -- their capacities for innovation.
sentences.zh: 第三部分是，尽管如此，我们都同意儿童拥有真正非凡的能力——他们的创新能力。

sentences.en: I mean, Sirena last night was a marvel, wasn't she?
sentences.zh: 我是说，昨晚的塞丽娜真是个奇迹，不是吗？

sentences.en: Just seeing what she could do. And she's exceptional, but I think she's not, so to speak, exceptional in the whole of childhood.
sentences.zh: 只是看看她能做什么。她很出色，但我认为她在整个童年时期并不出色。

sentences.en: What you have there is a person of extraordinary dedication who found a talent.
sentences.zh: 你所拥有的是一个具有非凡奉献精神并发现了才华的人。

sentences.en: And my contention is, all kids have tremendous talents, and we squander them, pretty ruthlessly.
sentences.zh: 我的观点是，所有的孩子都有巨大的才能，但我们却无情地浪费了他们。

sentences.en: So I want to talk about education, and I want to talk about creativity.
sentences.zh: 所以我想谈谈教育，我想谈谈创造力。

sentences.en: My contention is that creativity now is as important in education as literacy, and we should treat it with the same status.
sentences.zh: 我的观点是，现在创造力在教育中与识字能力一样重要，我们应该同等对待它。

sentences.en: (Applause) Thank you. (Applause) That was it, by the way. Thank you very much.
sentences.zh: （鼓掌）谢谢。 （掌声）顺便说一句，就是这样。非常感谢。

sentences.en: (Laughter) So, 15 minutes left. (Laughter) "Well, I was born ... "
sentences.zh: （笑声） 那么，还剩 15 分钟。 （笑声）“好吧，我出生了……”

sentences.en: (Laughter) I heard a great story recently -- I love telling it -- of a little girl who was in a drawing lesson.
sentences.zh: （笑声）我最近听到了一个很棒的故事——我喜欢讲这个故事——一个正在上绘画课的小女孩。

sentences.en: She was six, and she was at the back, drawing, and the teacher said this girl hardly ever paid attention, and in this drawing lesson, she did.
sentences.zh: 她六岁，在后面画画，老师说这个女孩几乎没有集中注意力，而在这堂绘画课上，她集中注意力了。

sentences.en: The teacher was fascinated. She went over to her, and she said, "What are you drawing?"
sentences.zh: 老师很着迷。她走到她身边，问道：“你在画什么？”

sentences.en: And the girl said, "I'm drawing a picture of God."
sentences.zh: 女孩说：“我正在画上帝的画像。”

sentences.en: And the teacher said, "But nobody knows what God looks like."
sentences.zh: 老师说：“但是没有人知道上帝长什么样。”

sentences.en: And the girl said, "They will in a minute."
sentences.zh: 女孩说：“一会儿就会的。”

sentences.en: (Laughter) When my son was four in England --
sentences.zh: （笑声）当我儿子四岁时在英国——

sentences.en: actually, he was four everywhere, to be honest.
sentences.zh: 事实上，说实话，他到处都是四岁。

sentences.en: (Laughter) If we're being strict about it, wherever he went, he was four that year.
sentences.zh: （笑声）如果我们严格来说，无论他去哪里，那一年他才四岁。

sentences.en: He was in the Nativity play. Do you remember the story?
sentences.zh: 他参加了耶稣诞生剧。你还记得这个故事吗？

sentences.en: (Laughter) No, it was big, it was a big story.
sentences.zh: （笑声）不，它很大，这是一个很大的故事。

sentences.en: Mel Gibson did the sequel, you may have seen it.
sentences.zh: 梅尔·吉布森制作了续集，你可能已经看过了。

sentences.en: (Laughter) "Nativity II." But James got the part of Joseph, which we were thrilled about.
sentences.zh: （笑声）《耶稣诞生二》。但詹姆斯得到了约瑟夫的角色，这让我们很兴奋。

sentences.en: We considered this to be one of the lead parts.
sentences.zh: 我们认为这是主要部分之一。

sentences.en: We had the place crammed full of agents in T-shirts: "James Robinson IS Joseph!"
sentences.zh: 我们的地方挤满了穿着 T 恤的特工：“詹姆斯·罗宾逊就是约瑟夫！”

sentences.en: (Laughter) He didn't have to speak, but you know the bit where the three kings come in?
sentences.zh: （笑声）他不必说话，但你知道三位国王是从哪里进来的吗？

sentences.en: They come in bearing gifts, gold, frankincense and myrrh.
sentences.zh: 他们带着礼物而来：黄金、乳香和没药。

sentences.en: This really happened. We were sitting there, and I think they just went out of sequence, because we talked to the little boy afterward and said, "You OK with that?" They said, "Yeah, why? Was that wrong?"
sentences.zh: 这确实发生了。我们坐在那里，我认为他们只是打乱了顺序，因为我们后来和那个小男孩交谈并说：“你同意吗？”他们说：“是啊，为什么？那是错的吗？”

sentences.en: They just switched. The three boys came in, four-year-olds with tea towels on their heads.
sentences.zh: 他们刚刚换了。三个男孩进来了，都是四岁的孩子，头上顶着茶巾。

sentences.en: They put these boxes down, and the first boy said, "I bring you gold."
sentences.zh: 他们把这些盒子放下，第一个男孩说：“我给你带来了金子。”

sentences.en: And the second boy said, "I bring you myrrh."
sentences.zh: 第二个男孩说：“我给你带来没药。”

sentences.en: And the third boy said, "Frank sent this."
sentences.zh: 第三个男孩说：“弗兰克寄来了这个。”

sentences.en: (Laughter) What these things have in common is that kids will take a chance.
sentences.zh: （笑声）这些事情的共同点是孩子们会冒险。

sentences.en: If they don't know, they'll have a go. Am I right? They're not frightened of being wrong.
sentences.zh: 如果他们不知道，他们就会尝试。我说得对吗？他们并不害怕犯错。

sentences.en: I don't mean to say that being wrong is the same thing as being creative.
sentences.zh: 我并不是说犯错和有创造力是一回事。

sentences.en: What we do know is, if you're not prepared to be wrong, you'll never come up with anything original -- if you're not prepared to be wrong.
sentences.zh: 我们所知道的是，如果你不准备犯错，你就永远不会想出任何原创的东西——如果你不准备犯错。

sentences.en: And by the time they get to be adults, most kids have lost that capacity.
sentences.zh: 当他们成年时，大多数孩子已经失去了这种能力。

sentences.en: They have become frightened of being wrong.
sentences.zh: 他们变得害怕犯错。

sentences.en: And we run our companies like this. We stigmatize mistakes.
sentences.zh: 我们就是这样经营我们的公司的。我们污蔑错误。

sentences.en: And we're now running national education systems where mistakes are the worst thing you can make.
sentences.zh: 我们现在运行的国家教育系统中，错误是最糟糕的事情。

sentences.en: And the result is that we are educating people out of their creative capacities.
sentences.zh: 结果是我们正在教育人们发挥他们的创造力。

sentences.en: Picasso once said this, he said that all children are born artists.
sentences.zh: 毕加索曾经说过这样的话，他说所有的孩子都是天生的艺术家。

sentences.en: The problem is to remain an artist as we grow up.
sentences.zh: 问题是随着我们的成长，我们仍然是一名艺术家。

sentences.en: I believe this passionately, that we don't grow into creativity, we grow out of it.
sentences.zh: 我坚信这一点：我们不是从创造力中成长起来的，而是从创造力中成长出来的。

sentences.en: Or rather, we get educated out of it. So why is this?
sentences.zh: 或者更确切地说，我们从中得到了教育。那么这是为什么呢？

sentences.en: I lived in Stratford-on-Avon until about five years ago.
sentences.zh: 大约五年前，我一直住在埃文河畔斯特拉特福。

sentences.en: In fact, we moved from Stratford to Los Angeles.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我们从斯特拉特福搬到了洛杉矶。

sentences.en: So you can imagine what a seamless transition this was.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以想象这是一个多么无缝的过渡。

sentences.en: (Laughter) Actually, we lived in a place called Snitterfield, just outside Stratford, which is where Shakespeare's father was born.
sentences.zh: （笑声） 事实上，我们住在斯特拉特福郊外一个叫斯尼特菲尔德的地方，那是莎士比亚父亲的出生地。

sentences.en: Are you struck by a new thought? I was. You don't think of Shakespeare having a father, do you?
sentences.zh: 您有新的想法吗？我是。你不认为莎士比亚有父亲，是吗？

sentences.en: Do you? Because you don't think of Shakespeare being a child, do you?
sentences.zh: 你？因为你不认为莎士比亚是个孩子，是吗？

sentences.en: Shakespeare being seven? I never thought of it.
sentences.zh: 莎士比亚七岁？我从来没有想过。

sentences.en: I mean, he was seven at some point. He was in somebody's English class, wasn't he?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他在某个时候七岁。他在某人的英语课上，不是吗？

sentences.en: (Laughter) How annoying would that be? (Laughter) "Must try harder."
sentences.zh: （笑声） 那会有多烦人呢？ （笑声）“必须更加努力。”

sentences.en: (Laughter) Being sent to bed by his dad, to Shakespeare, "Go to bed, now!"
sentences.zh: （笑声） 被他爸爸送去睡觉，对莎士比亚说：“现在就去睡觉！”

sentences.en: To William Shakespeare. "And put the pencil down!"
sentences.zh: 献给威廉·莎士比亚。 “把铅笔放下！”

sentences.en: (Laughter) "And stop speaking like that."
sentences.zh: （笑声）“别再这样说话了。”

sentences.en: (Laughter) "It's confusing everybody." (Laughter) Anyway, we moved from Stratford to Los Angeles,
sentences.zh: （笑声）“这让每个人都感到困惑。” （笑声）不管怎样，我们从斯特拉特福搬到了洛杉矶，

sentences.en: and I just want to say a word about the transition.
sentences.zh: 我只想就过渡说几句话。

sentences.en: Actually, my son didn't want to come. I've got two kids; he's 21 now, my daughter's 16.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我儿子不想来。我有两个孩子；他现在21岁，我女儿16岁。

sentences.en: He didn't want to come to Los Angeles. He loved it, but he had a girlfriend in England.
sentences.zh: 他不想来洛杉矶。他很喜欢，但他在英国有一个女朋友。

sentences.en: This was the love of his life, Sarah. He'd known her for a month.
sentences.zh: 这是他一生的挚爱，莎拉。他认识她一个月了。

sentences.en: (Laughter) Mind you, they'd had their fourth anniversary, because it's a long time when you're 16.
sentences.zh: （笑声）请注意，他们已经过了四周年纪念日，因为对于 16 岁的人来说这是一段很长的时间。

sentences.en: He was really upset on the plane. He said, "I'll never find another girl like Sarah."
sentences.zh: 他在飞机上真的很沮丧。他说：“我再也找不到像莎拉这样的女孩了。”

sentences.en: And we were rather pleased about that, frankly -- (Laughter) because she was the main reason we were leaving the country.
sentences.zh: 坦率地说，我们对此感到非常高兴——（笑声）因为她是我们离开这个国家的主要原因。

sentences.en: (Laughter) But something strikes you when you move to America and travel around the world: every education system on earth has the same hierarchy of subjects.
sentences.zh: （笑声）但是当你搬到美国并环游世界时，有件事会让你震惊：地球上的每个教育系统都有相同的科目等级。

sentences.en: Every one. Doesn't matter where you go. You'd think it would be otherwise, but it isn't.
sentences.zh: 每个人。你去哪里并不重要。你可能会认为情况会是另外一种情况，但事实并非如此。

sentences.en: At the top are mathematics and languages, then the humanities.
sentences.zh: 最上面的是数学和语言，然后是人文学科。

sentences.en: At the bottom are the arts. Everywhere on earth.
sentences.zh: 最底层的是艺术。地球上到处都是。

sentences.en: And in pretty much every system, too, there's a hierarchy within the arts.
sentences.zh: 几乎在每个系统中，艺术内部也存在等级制度。

sentences.en: Art and music are normally given a higher status in schools than drama and dance.
sentences.zh: 艺术和音乐在学校中的地位通常高于戏剧和舞蹈。

sentences.en: There isn't an education system on the planet that teaches dance every day to children the way we teach them mathematics.
sentences.zh: 世界上没有一个教育系统能够像教数学一样每天教孩子们舞蹈。

sentences.en: Why? Why not? I think this is rather important.
sentences.zh: 为什么？为什么不呢？我觉得这个还是比较重要的。

sentences.en: I think math is very important, but so is dance.
sentences.zh: 我认为数学很重要，但舞蹈也很重要。

sentences.en: Children dance all the time if they're allowed to, we all do.
sentences.zh: 如果允许的话，孩子们总是会跳舞，我们都这样做。

sentences.en: We all have bodies, don't we? Did I miss a meeting?
sentences.zh: 我们都有身体，不是吗？我错过了一个会议吗？

sentences.en: (Laughter) Truthfully, what happens is, as children grow up, we start to educate them progressively from the waist up.
sentences.zh: （笑声）说实话，随着孩子的成长，我们开始从腰部以上逐步教育他们。

sentences.en: And then we focus on their heads. And slightly to one side.
sentences.zh: 然后我们把注意力集中在他们的头上。并且稍微偏向一侧。

sentences.en: If you were to visit education as an alien and say "What's it for, public education?"
sentences.zh: 如果你以外星人的身份参观教育并说“公共教育是为了什么？”

sentences.en: I think you'd have to conclude, if you look at the output, who really succeeds by this, who does everything they should, who gets all the brownie points, who are the winners -- I think you'd have to conclude the whole purpose of public education
sentences.zh: 我想你必须得出结论，如果你看看结果，谁真正成功了，谁做了他们应该做的一切，谁得到了所有的布朗尼点，谁是赢家——我认为你必须得出结论公共教育的全部目的

sentences.en: throughout the world is to produce university professors.
sentences.zh: 全世界都在培养大学教授。

sentences.en: Isn't it? They're the people who come out the top.
sentences.zh: 不是吗？他们是那些脱颖而出的人。

sentences.en: And I used to be one, so there. (Laughter) And I like university professors, but, you know, we shouldn't hold them up as the high-water mark of all human achievement.
sentences.zh: 我曾经也是其中之一，所以就在那里。 （笑声）我喜欢大学教授，但是，你知道，我们不应该把他们视为所有人类成就的最高点。

sentences.en: They're just a form of life. Another form of life.
sentences.zh: 它们只是生命的一种形式。生命的另一种形式。

sentences.en: But they're rather curious. And I say this out of affection for them: there's something curious about professors.
sentences.zh: 但他们很好奇。我这样说是出于对他们的喜爱：教授们有些好奇。

sentences.en: In my experience -- not all of them, but typically -- they live in their heads.
sentences.zh: 根据我的经验——不是全部，但通常是——他们生活在自己的头脑中。

sentences.en: They live up there and slightly to one side.
sentences.zh: 他们住在那儿，稍微偏向一侧。

sentences.en: They're disembodied, you know, in a kind of literal way.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们在某种程度上是脱离实体的。

sentences.en: They look upon their body as a form of transport for their heads.
sentences.zh: 他们将身体视为头部的一种交通工具。

sentences.en: (Laughter) Don't they? It's a way of getting their head to meetings.
sentences.zh: （笑声） 不是吗？这是让他们集中精力参加会议的一种方式。

sentences.en: (Laughter) If you want real evidence of out-of-body experiences, by the way, get yourself along to a residential conference of senior academics
sentences.zh: （笑声）如果你想要灵魂出窍经历的真实证据，顺便说一句，参加一个由高级学者组成的住宿会议

sentences.en: and pop into the discotheque on the final night.
sentences.zh: 并在最后一晚走进迪斯科舞厅。

sentences.en: (Laughter) And there, you will see it. Grown men and women writhing uncontrollably, off the beat.
sentences.zh: （笑声） 在那里，你会看到它。成年男女无法控制地扭动，失去节拍。

sentences.en: (Laughter) Waiting until it ends, so they can go home and write a paper about it.
sentences.zh: （笑声）等到它结束，这样他们就可以回家写一篇关于它的论文。

sentences.en: (Laughter) Our education system is predicated on the idea of academic ability.
sentences.zh: （笑声）我们的教育体系是以学术能力为基础的。

sentences.en: And there's a reason. Around the world, there were no public systems of education, really, before the 19th century.
sentences.zh: 这是有原因的。事实上，在 19 世纪之前，世界各地都没有公共教育系统。

sentences.en: They all came into being to meet the needs of industrialism.
sentences.zh: 它们都是为了适应工业化的需要而产生的。

sentences.en: So the hierarchy is rooted on two ideas.
sentences.zh: 因此，层次结构植根于两个想法。

sentences.en: Number one, that the most useful subjects for work are at the top.
sentences.zh: 第一，对工作最有用的主题位于顶部。

sentences.en: So you were probably steered benignly away from things at school when you were a kid, things you liked, on the grounds you would never get a job doing that.
sentences.zh: 所以当你还是个孩子的时候，你可能会被善意地引导远离学校里的东西，远离你喜欢的东西，因为你永远找不到这样做的工作。

sentences.en: Is that right? "Don't do music, you're not going to be a musician; don't do art, you won't be an artist."
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？ “不做音乐，你不会成为音乐家；不做艺术，你不会成为艺术家。”

sentences.en: Benign advice -- now, profoundly mistaken.
sentences.zh: 善意的建议——现在看来是大错特错了。

sentences.en: The whole world is engulfed in a revolution.
sentences.zh: 整个世界都陷入了一场革命。

sentences.en: And the second is academic ability, which has really come to dominate our view of intelligence, because the universities design the system in their image.
sentences.zh: 第二个是学术能力，它确实主导了我们对智力的看法，因为大学按照自己的形象设计了系统。

sentences.en: If you think of it, the whole system of public education around the world is a protracted process of university entrance.
sentences.zh: 如果你想一想，世界各地的整个公共教育体系都是一个漫长的大学入学过程。

sentences.en: And the consequence is that many highly talented, brilliant, creative people think they're not, because the thing they were good at school wasn't valued, or was actually stigmatized.
sentences.zh: 结果是，许多才华横溢、才华横溢、富有创造力的人认为自己不是，因为他们在学校擅长的事情没有得到重视，或者实际上受到了侮辱。

sentences.en: And I think we can't afford to go on that way.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们不能再这样下去了。

sentences.en: In the next 30 years, according to UNESCO, more people worldwide will be graduating through education than since the beginning of history.
sentences.zh: 据联合国教科文组织称，未来 30 年，全世界通过教育毕业的人数将比历史开始以来还要多。

sentences.en: More people. And it's the combination of all the things we've talked about: technology and its transformational effect on work, and demography and the huge explosion in population.
sentences.zh: 更多人。这是我们讨论过的所有事情的结合：技术及其对工作的变革性影响，以及人口统计和人口的巨大爆炸。

sentences.en: Suddenly, degrees aren't worth anything.
sentences.zh: 突然间，学位变得毫无价值。

sentences.en: Isn't that true? When I was a student, if you had a degree, you had a job.
sentences.zh: 这不是真的吗？当我还是一名学生时，如果你有学位，你就有工作。

sentences.en: If you didn't have a job, it's because you didn't want one.
sentences.zh: 如果你没有工作，那是因为你不想要一份工作。

sentences.en: And I didn't want one, frankly. (Laughter) But now kids with degrees are often heading home to carry on playing video games, because you need an MA where the previous job required a BA,
sentences.zh: 坦白说，我并不想要一个。 （笑声）但是现在有学位的孩子经常回家继续玩电子游戏，因为你需要硕士学位，而以前的工作需要学士学位，

sentences.en: and now you need a PhD for the other. It's a process of academic inflation.
sentences.zh: 现在你需要另一个博士学位。这是一个学术膨胀的过程。

sentences.en: And it indicates the whole structure of education is shifting beneath our feet.
sentences.zh: 这表明整个教育结构正在我们脚下发生变化。

sentences.en: We need to radically rethink our view of intelligence.
sentences.zh: 我们需要从根本上重新思考我们对情报的看法。

sentences.en: We know three things about intelligence.
sentences.zh: 我们知道关于智力的三件事。

sentences.en: One, it's diverse. We think about the world in all the ways that we experience it.
sentences.zh: 一、它是多样化的。我们以我们体验世界的各种方式思考这个世界。

sentences.en: We think visually, we think in sound, we think kinesthetically.
sentences.zh: 我们用视觉思考、用声音思考、用动觉思考。

sentences.en: We think in abstract terms, we think in movement.
sentences.zh: 我们以抽象的方式思考，我们以运动的方式思考。

sentences.en: Secondly, intelligence is dynamic. If you look at the interactions of a human brain, as we heard yesterday from a number of presentations, intelligence is wonderfully interactive.
sentences.zh: 其次，智力是动态的。如果你观察一下人脑的相互作用，正如我们昨天从许多演讲中听到的那样，智能是具有奇妙的交互性的。

sentences.en: The brain isn't divided into compartments.
sentences.zh: 大脑不分为区室。

sentences.en: In fact, creativity -- which I define as the process of having original ideas that have value -- more often than not comes about through the interaction of different disciplinary ways of seeing things.
sentences.zh: 事实上，创造力——我将其定义为产生有价值的原创想法的过程——通常是通过不同学科看待事物的方式的相互作用而产生的。

sentences.en: By the way, there's a shaft of nerves that joins the two halves of the brain, called the corpus callosum.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一下，有一条神经连接大脑的两半，称为胼胝体。

sentences.en: It's thicker in women. Following off from Helen yesterday, this is probably why women are better at multitasking.
sentences.zh: 女性则较厚。继昨天的海伦之后，这可能就是女性更擅长同时处理多项任务的原因。

sentences.en: Because you are, aren't you? There's a raft of research, but I know it from my personal life.
sentences.zh: 因为你就是，不是吗？有大量的研究，但我从我的个人生活中知道了这一点。

sentences.en: If my wife is cooking a meal at home, which is not often ...
sentences.zh: 如果我妻子在家做饭，这并不常见......

sentences.en: thankfully. (Laughter) No, she's good at some things.
sentences.zh: 谢天谢地。 （笑声）不，她在某些事情上很擅长。

sentences.en: But if she's cooking, she's dealing with people on the phone, she's talking to the kids, she's painting the ceiling -- (Laughter) she's doing open-heart surgery over here.
sentences.zh: 但如果她正在做饭，她正在打电话与人打交道，她正在与孩子们交谈，她正在粉刷天花板 - （笑声）她正在这里进行心脏直视手术。

sentences.en: If I'm cooking, the door is shut, the kids are out, the phone's on the hook, if she comes in, I get annoyed.
sentences.zh: 如果我正在做饭，门就关上了，孩子们出去了，电话挂断了，如果她进来，我就会生气。

sentences.en: I say, "Terry, please, I'm trying to fry an egg in here."
sentences.zh: 我说：“特里，拜托，我想在这里煎一个鸡蛋。”

sentences.en: (Laughter) "Give me a break." (Laughter) Actually, do you know that old philosophical thing,
sentences.zh: （笑声）“让我休息一下。” （笑声）事实上，你知道那个古老的哲学道理吗？

sentences.en: "If a tree falls in a forest, and nobody hears it, did it happen?"
sentences.zh: “如果一棵树倒在森林里，没有人听到，这真的发生了吗？”

sentences.en: Remember that old chestnut? I saw a great T-shirt recently, which said, "If a man speaks his mind in a forest, and no woman hears him, is he still wrong?"
sentences.zh: 还记得那个老栗子吗？我最近看到一件很棒的T恤，上面写着：“如果一个男人在森林里说出自己的想法，而没有女人听到他的声音，那么他还是错了吗？”

sentences.en: (Laughter) And the third thing about intelligence is, it's distinct.
sentences.zh: （笑声） 关于智力的第三点是，它是独特的。

sentences.en: I'm doing a new book at the moment called "Epiphany," which is based on a series of interviews with people about how they discovered their talent.
sentences.zh: 我目前正在写一本名为《顿悟》的新书，该书基于对人们如何发现自己的才能的一系列采访。

sentences.en: I'm fascinated by how people got to be there.
sentences.zh: 我对人们如何到达那里感到着迷。

sentences.en: It's really prompted by a conversation I had with a wonderful woman who maybe most people have never heard of, Gillian Lynne.
sentences.zh: 这实际上是由我与一位可能大多数人从未听说过的出色女性吉莉安·林恩 (Gillian Lynne) 的一次对话引发的。

sentences.en: Have you heard of her? Some have. She's a choreographer, and everybody knows her work.
sentences.zh: 你听说过她吗？有些有。她是一名编舞家，每个人都知道她的工作。

sentences.en: She did "Cats" and "Phantom of the Opera."
sentences.zh: 她出演了《猫》和《歌剧魅影》。

sentences.en: She's wonderful. I used to be on the board of The Royal Ballet, as you can see.
sentences.zh: 她很棒。如你所见，我曾经是皇家芭蕾舞团的董事会成员。

sentences.en: (Laughter) Gillian and I had lunch one day. I said, "How did you get to be a dancer?"
sentences.zh: （笑声） 有一天，阿娇和我共进午餐。我说：“你是怎么成为一名舞者的？”

sentences.en: It was interesting. When she was at school, she was really hopeless.
sentences.zh: 这很有趣。当她在学校的时候，她真的很绝望。

sentences.en: And the school, in the '30s, wrote to her parents and said, "We think Gillian has a learning disorder."
sentences.zh: 三十年代，学校写信给她的父母说：“我们认为阿娇有学习障碍。”

sentences.en: She couldn't concentrate; she was fidgeting.
sentences.zh: 她无法集中注意力；她坐立不安。

sentences.en: I think now they'd say she had ADHD. Wouldn't you?
sentences.zh: 我想现在他们会说她患有多动症。你不会吗？

sentences.en: But this was the 1930s, and ADHD hadn't been invented at this point.
sentences.zh: 但那是 20 世纪 30 年代，此时 ADHD 还没有被发明。

sentences.en: It wasn't an available condition. (Laughter) People weren't aware they could have that.
sentences.zh: 这不是一个可用的条件。 （笑声）人们并不知道他们可以拥有它。

sentences.en: (Laughter) Anyway, she went to see this specialist.
sentences.zh: （笑声）不管怎样，她还是去看了这位专家。

sentences.en: So, this oak-paneled room, and she was there with her mother, and she was led and sat on this chair at the end, and she sat on her hands for 20 minutes, while this man talked to her mother about all the problems Gillian was having at school,
sentences.zh: 所以，在这个橡木镶板的房间里，她和她的母亲在一起，她被引导坐在最后的这张椅子上，她用手坐了20分钟，而这个男人和她的母亲谈论了吉莉安在学校遇到的所有问题，

sentences.en: because she was disturbing people, her homework was always late, and so on.
sentences.zh: 因为她打扰别人，她的作业总是迟到等等。

sentences.en: Little kid of eight. In the end, the doctor went and sat next to Gillian and said, "I've listened to all these things your mother's told me.
sentences.zh: 八岁的小孩子。最后，医生走到阿娇身边坐下，说道：“你妈妈告诉我的这些事情我都听了。

sentences.en: I need to speak to her privately. Wait here. We'll be back. We won't be very long," and they went and left her.
sentences.zh: 我需要和她私下谈谈。在这里等一下。我们会回来的。我们不会待太久的。”然后他们就离开了她。

sentences.en: But as they went out of the room, he turned on the radio that was sitting on his desk.
sentences.zh: 但当他们走出房间时，他打开了办公桌上的收音机。

sentences.en: And when they got out of the room, he said to her mother, "Just stand and watch her."
sentences.zh: 当他们走出房间时，他对她母亲说：“站着看着她。”

sentences.en: And the minute they left the room, she was on her feet, moving to the music.
sentences.zh: 他们一离开房间，她就站了起来，随着音乐移动。

sentences.en: And they watched for a few minutes, and he turned to her mother and said, "Mrs. Lynne, Gillian isn't sick.
sentences.zh: 他们看了几分钟，然后他转向她的母亲说：“林恩夫人，吉莉安没有生病。

sentences.en: She's a dancer. Take her to a dance school."
sentences.zh: 她是一名舞者。带她去舞蹈学校。”

sentences.en: I said, "What happened?" She said, "She did. I can't tell you how wonderful it was.
sentences.zh: 我说：“发生什么事了？”她说：“她做到了。我无法告诉你那有多美妙。

sentences.en: We walked in this room, and it was full of people like me -- people who couldn't sit still, people who had to move to think."
sentences.zh: 我们走进这个房间，里面挤满了像我这样的人——那些坐不住的人，那些必须动起来思考的人。”

sentences.en: Who had to move to think. They did ballet, they did tap, jazz; they did modern; they did contemporary.
sentences.zh: 谁必须动起来思考。他们跳芭蕾、踢踏舞、爵士乐；他们做的是现代的；他们做了当代的。

sentences.en: She was eventually auditioned for the Royal Ballet School.
sentences.zh: 她最终参加了皇家芭蕾舞学校的试镜。

sentences.en: She became a soloist; she had a wonderful career at the Royal Ballet.
sentences.zh: 她成为一名独奏家；她在皇家芭蕾舞团有着辉煌的职业生涯。

sentences.en: She eventually graduated from the Royal Ballet School, founded the Gillian Lynne Dance Company, met Andrew Lloyd Webber.
sentences.zh: 她最终从皇家芭蕾舞学校毕业，创立了吉莉安·林恩舞蹈团，结识了安德鲁·劳埃德·韦伯。

sentences.en: She's been responsible for some of the most successful musical theater productions in history, she's given pleasure to millions, and she's a multimillionaire.
sentences.zh: 她创作了一些历史上最成功的音乐剧作品，为数百万人带来了欢乐，而且她还是一位千万富翁。

sentences.en: Somebody else might have put her on medication and told her to calm down.
sentences.zh: 其他人可能会让她服用药物并告诉她冷静下来。

sentences.en: (Applause) What I think it comes to is this: Al Gore spoke the other night about ecology and the revolution that was triggered by Rachel Carson.
sentences.zh: （掌声）我认为事情是这样的：前几天晚上阿尔·戈尔谈到了生态学和雷切尔·卡森引发的革命。

sentences.en: I believe our only hope for the future is to adopt a new conception of human ecology, one in which we start to reconstitute our conception of the richness of human capacity.
sentences.zh: 我相信，我们未来的唯一希望是采用一种新的人类生态学概念，开始重建我们对人类能力丰富性的概念。

sentences.en: Our education system has mined our minds in the way that we strip-mine the earth for a particular commodity.
sentences.zh: 我们的教育体系挖掘了我们的思想，就像我们在地球上开采某种特定商品一样。

sentences.en: And for the future, it won't serve us. We have to rethink the fundamental principles on which we're educating our children.
sentences.zh: 对于未来，它不会为我们服务。我们必须重新思考我们教育孩子的基本原则。

sentences.en: There was a wonderful quote by Jonas Salk, who said, "If all the insects were to disappear from the Earth, within 50 years, all life on Earth would end.
sentences.zh: 乔纳斯·索尔克（Jonas Salk）有一句精彩的话，他说：“如果所有的昆虫都从地球上消失，50年内，地球上的所有生命都将终结。

sentences.en: If all human beings disappeared from the Earth, within 50 years, all forms of life would flourish."
sentences.zh: 如果所有人类从地球上消失，50年内，所有形式的生命都会蓬勃发展。”

sentences.en: And he's right. What TED celebrates is the gift of the human imagination.
sentences.zh: 他是对的。 TED 庆祝的是人类想象力的礼物。

sentences.en: We have to be careful now that we use this gift wisely, and that we avert some of the scenarios that we've talked about.
sentences.zh: 我们现在必须小心，明智地使用这份礼物，并避免我们已经讨论过的一些情况。

sentences.en: And the only way we'll do it is by seeing our creative capacities for the richness they are and seeing our children for the hope that they are.
sentences.zh: 我们要做到这一点的唯一方法就是看到我们的创造力的丰富性，并看到我们的孩子的希望。

sentences.en: And our task is to educate their whole being, so they can face this future.
sentences.zh: 我们的任务是教育他们的整体，让他们能够面对这个未来。

sentences.en: By the way -- we may not see this future, but they will.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，我们可能看不到这样的未来，但他们会的。

sentences.en: And our job is to help them make something of it.
sentences.zh: 我们的工作就是帮助他们有所作为。

sentences.en: Thank you very much. (Applause)
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。 （掌声）
